title: Differential Centrifugation to Enrich Bacterial Ribonucleoprotein Bodies from Caulobacter crescentus
author: Muthunayake, Al-Husini, et al.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and media
steps.instruction: Prepare all required buffers and PYE growth medium in advance, ensuring they are RNase‑free (use DEPC‑treated water) and that sufficient volumes are available for the experiment.

steps.title: Streak strains on selective plates
steps.instruction: Streak JS299 and JS221 strains onto PYE agar plates containing 5 µg/mL kanamycin, 0.5 µg/mL gentamicin, 0.2 % xylose, and 1.5 % agar; incubate ~16 h at 28 °C.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend overnight culture
steps.instruction: Wash the overnight culture three times with PYE medium, then resuspend the washed cells in 5 mL fresh PYE.

steps.title: Measure initial optical density
steps.instruction: Take a 1 mL aliquot of the resuspended culture and measure OD600 using a cuvette with a 1 cm path length.

steps.title: Dilute culture to OD 0.05
steps.instruction: In a 125 mL Erlenmeyer flask add 30 mL PYE supplemented with 500 µM vanillate, 0.5 µg/mL gentamicin and 5 µg/mL kanamycin; dilute the culture to an OD600 of 0.05, mix well, and record the starting OD600 from a 1 mL aliquot.

steps.title: Incubate to mid‑exponential phase
steps.instruction: Incubate the flask at 28 °C with shaking at 250 rpm; measure OD600 every 2 h until it reaches approximately 0.4–0.6.

steps.title: Confirm BR‑body formation
steps.instruction: Spot 1 µL of each strain (JS299 and JS221) onto M2G agarose pads (1.5 % agarose), air‑dry, and image by phase‑contrast and YFP fluorescence to verify RNase E‑YFP foci before harvesting.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the culture to a 50 mL conical tube kept on ice, pellet at 11,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 2.5 mL ice‑cold lysis buffer.

steps.title: Freeze cell suspension
steps.instruction: Slowly drip the cell‑lysis buffer suspension into a 50 mL conical tube half‑filled with liquid nitrogen; puncture the lid with a hot needle, pour out excess liquid nitrogen, allow it to evaporate completely, replace the lid, and store the tube at –80 °C (use cryogenic gloves and face shield).
